I ran the simulation for all three technologies at 50, 150, and 300 µm, and recorded the results.

| Technology | 50 µm | 150 µm | 300 µm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sensor-T1 | 10.631 µm | 9.140 µm | 11.625 µm |
| Sensor-T2 | 6.909 µm | **6.224 µm** | 7.840 µm |
| Sensor-T3 | 16.791 µm | 13.710 µm | 19.633 µm |

Sensor-T2 at 150 µm gives the best unirradiated single-hit resolution. 150 µm is the best of the three thicknesses tested for every technology.

The radiation screen could not actually be applied. No document gives a fluence or dose requirement, so I advanced all three technologies without excluding any. These are unirradiated results only. Radiation damage matters for the innermost layer, and I have not simulated irradiated performance. I sampled only three thicknesses per technology, so the true optimum between them is not resolved.

content.text:
**Step s4 result: the radiation check could not be completed, so Sensor-T2 at 150 µm is provisional.**

I re-read the three documents most relevant to radiation (`simulation_summary_2025.md`, `meeting_notes_2026-03-02.md`, `readout_chip.md`). None of them gives a fluence or dose requirement, irradiated resolution, or radiation-tolerance data. That means no candidate can be confirmed or excluded on radiation grounds.

**Ranking by unirradiated single-hit resolution (µm):**
1. T2 @ 150 µm: 6.224 (leading candidate)
2. T2 @ 50 µm: 6.909
3. T2 @ 300 µm: 7.84
4. T1 @ 150 µm: 9.14
5. T1 @ 50 µm: 10.631
6. T1 @ 300 µm: 11.625
7. T3 @ 150 µm: 13.71
8. T3 @ 50 µm: 16.791
9. T3 @ 300 µm: 19.633

**Rationale and caveats:**
- Sensor-T2 at 150 µm gives the best unirradiated resolution. Its viability after irradiation is unverified.
- Charge-collection loss at high fluence generally favours thinner sensors. If the irradiated screen penalises 150 µm, T2 at 50 µm (6.909 µm unirradiated) is the fallback.
- T2 at 300 µm is the least attractive T2 option for radiation.
- Irradiated performance has not been simulated, and thickness was sampled at only three points per technology.
- Before a final recommendation, the fluence requirement at the innermost radius needs to be obtained, and irradiated resolution simulated for T2 at 50 and 150 µm.

The ranking and these caveats are recorded for later steps.

**Recommendation (provisional): Sensor-T2 (thin-pitch, large signal sharing) at 150 µm.** This is not a fully validated submission. The radiation constraint is unverified.

**Supporting resolution numbers (unirradiated, single-hit, from the simulation):**

| Technology | 50 µm | 150 µm | 300 µm |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sensor-T1 | 10.631 | 9.140 | 11.625 |
| **Sensor-T2** | 6.909 | **6.224** | 7.840 |
| Sensor-T3 | 16.791 | 13.710 | 19.633 |

Sensor-T2 is the best technology at every thickness, and 150 µm is the best thickness for every technology. T2 at 150 µm gives the best resolution of the nine points tested.

**Radiation justification: not established.** The project documents contain no fluence or dose requirement for the innermost layer, no irradiated resolution data, and no radiation-tolerance information. I therefore could not confirm or exclude any technology on radiation grounds, which is a stated constraint. The only basis for a thickness choice is general sensor physics: charge-collection loss at high fluence usually favours thinner sensors. On that basis, T2 at 50 µm is the safer fallback. It costs about 0.7 µm of resolution (6.909 vs 6.224 µm) and is the better choice if irradiated simulations penalise 150 µm.

**Caveats:**
- All resolution numbers are for unirradiated sensors. The simulation tool does not model irradiation, so the innermost-layer performance is unknown.
- Thickness was sampled at only three points per technology. The true optimum between 50 and 300 µm is not resolved.
- Before final sign-off, the project needs to supply the fluence requirement at the innermost radius. Irradiated resolution should then be simulated for T2 at 50 µm and 150 µm, and the choice made from those results.

It gives the best unirradiated single-hit resolution of the nine technology/thickness points simulated (6.224 um, versus 6.909 um at 50 um and 7.840 um at 300 um for T2; T1 best is 9.140 um and T3 best is 13.710 um). T2 is best at every thickness, and 150 um is the best thickness for every technology. The radiation constraint is NOT verified. No project document gives a fluence or dose requirement at the innermost radius, and the simulation does not model irradiated performance, so radiation suitability of all three technologies is unknown and none could be excluded. The stated goal is best resolution, so 150 um is chosen, but this choice should be treated as conditional. If irradiated simulations or the fluence requirement show charge-collection loss at 150 um, the fallback is T2 at 50 um (6.909 um unirradiated, about 0.7 um worse). Thickness was sampled at only three points per technology, so the true optimum between 50 and 300 um is not resolved. Before final sign-off, obtain the innermost-layer fluence requirement and simulate irradiated resolution for T2 at 50 and 150 um.
